A moved partial is a classic way to lose the token. Likely causes: the partial's `<form>` no longer has `{% csrf_token %}` inside it, the partial is rendered without the request (so the token comes out empty), or an `hx-headers` carrying `X-CSRFToken` was on an element that no longer wraps the form. I'd check in the Network tab whether the POST carries `X-CSRFToken` or a `csrfmiddlewaretoken` field at all.
Action: Ask you to paste the partial and the view that renders it (or look at them in trailmix), and I'll pinpoint which of those it is.

A 403 CSRF failure after moving the form into a partial usually means the POST no longer carries the token: either the partial dropped {% csrf_token %} from inside the form, or it's rendered without the request context so the tag comes out empty. The fix is to put {% csrf_token %} inside the form in the partial, or send the token on every htmx request with hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}' on the body. Action: look at the partial and how the view renders it in trailmix; paste them if you'd rather check yourself.

A common cause: htmx requests only carry the CSRF token if it's in the request, and moving the form into a partial may have dropped the token from the form itself. Putting {% csrf_token %} inside the form in the partial, or sending the token via hx-headers on the body, fixes it. I haven't seen your templates, so that's the first thing to check.
Action: I'd open the partial and the view, confirm the token is rendered inside the form (and the partial is rendered with the request), and add it if not.

htmx doesn't add the CSRF token on its own, so moving the form probably left the token out of the request. Common causes: the form no longer contains `{% csrf_token %}`, the base template sends it via `hx-headers` on an element that isn't an ancestor of the swapped partial, or the partial is rendered without the request context so the token is empty. Easiest check: look at the failing request in the Network tab for `csrfmiddlewaretoken` or `X-CSRFToken`.
